distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Local mat, boundary, display, and calibration requirements are documented; remote-site safety equivalence is not.

sensing_tracking.summary: Full-body motion tracking is constitutive.

measurement.summary: The system converts tracked movement into health, damage, and round outcomes.

comparability.summary: Rules and common equipment support comparison, but calibration, patch, and remote latency controls are not fully public.

officiation.summary: Software, referees, and certified match operators jointly administer matches.

outcome_openness.summary: Round outcomes depend on live tracked performance.

consequence_structure.summary: Round wins, match advancement, and championship medals derive from contest structure.

operational_spatial_integration.summary: The co-located contest is strongly spatial-athletic. The planned test of geographically distributed performance remains unresolved rather than inferred from global availability.

human_limits_accessibility.note: Non-contact format reduces contact risk but introduces headset and motion risks.

source_provisional_finding.summary: Virtual Taekwondo supports the Spatial Athletic Contest class for co-located competition. Sprint 5 does not establish a remote distributed arena because current primary evidence does not demonstrate that configuration.

content: Published remote match rules, latency budgets, calibration procedures, and evidence of competitors in different physical sites sharing one match.

classified_object.notes: The object is the regulated rehabilitation product and supervised exercise configuration, not stroke rehabilitation as a whole and not a competitive sport.

performance_agency.summary: The patient must generate goal-directed movement during each exercise; performance agency exists without a competitive opponent.

performance_interface.summary: Motion capture and a computer-based interface translate patient movement into interactive tasks and feedback.

embodied_performance.summary: Adaptive bodily performance, fine motor control, sensorimotor coordination, and tracked movement are the therapeutic channel.

arena.summary: A computer-mediated exercise environment structures targets and feedback but does not constitute a sport arena.

distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Motion capture and therapeutic software synchronize movement and feedback.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Clinical setup and patient-specific calibration govern the exercise.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: No sport officiation; clinical supervision governs protocol.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Clinical responsibility and patient suitability are central.

sensing_tracking.summary: Motion capture detects patient movement.

measurement.summary: Clinical scales and system task data can measure movement and progress.

comparability.summary: Clinical comparison requires protocol, population, dose, assessor, and outcome alignment; product scores alone are insufficient.

officiation.summary: A therapist supervises care, but sport officiation does not apply.

outcome_openness.summary: Therapeutic task completion is not an open competitive outcome.

consequence_structure.summary: Functional progress, adherence, fatigue, and clinical risk are meaningful consequences, but not contest consequences.

operational_spatial_integration.summary: The system is strongly embodied and computationally mediated, but its correct class is Spatial Support System because therapeutic purpose and protocol replace contest structure.

participatory_actor_relations.action_window: Before and during the therapeutic exercise.
participatory_actor_relations.mechanism: The clinician selects or adjusts protocol parameters and supervises safe execution.
participatory_actor_relations.resource_or_constraint_effect: The supervisor changes task conditions without performing the patient's movement.
participatory_actor_relations.uncertainty: Clinical roles and software permissions may vary by deployment.

human_limits_accessibility.note: Clinical suitability, fatigue, and impairment variation govern use.

source_provisional_finding.summary: This case strongly validates the Spatial Support System sibling class: embodied spatial interaction can be clinically meaningful without being sport or contest.

content: A separately governed competitive event using the same technical platform with open outcomes and contest rules.

classified_object.notes: The object is the CYBATHLON EXO contest, where a pilot and exoskeleton complete physical tasks; individual devices may use different control modes.

performance_agency.summary: Pilot skill and decisions matter, but permitted manual, semi-autonomous, and autonomous modes can shift causal control during tasks.

performance_interface.summary: A robotic exoskeleton is an adaptive assistive interface that may interpret input or environment state.

embodied_performance.summary: Adaptive bodily performance, balance, cognitive control, and assisted locomotion are constitutive.

arena.summary: Physical task courses contain variable obstacles and everyday activity challenges.

distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Not applicable.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Device-specific control and assistance remain relevant to comparability, but not as a distributed-arena relation.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Officials evaluate task completion and time on the physical course.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Pilot, assistive device, and course safety are local and constitutive.

sensing_tracking.summary: Devices may use environment sensing and intention detection; implementations vary.

measurement.summary: Task completion and time are recorded under competition rules.

comparability.summary: Rules create a common task frame, but assistance architectures differ substantially.

officiation.summary: Competition officials administer task completion and results.

outcome_openness.summary: Results emerge from pilot–device performance under task constraints.

consequence_structure.summary: Task success, time, ranking, and awards follow from competition.

operational_spatial_integration.summary: The contest is deeply human–machine mediated, but the arena remains physical. Assistance and agency handoff—not computational Spatiality—are the primary analytical pressures.

human_limits_accessibility.note: Safety and disability-specific access are constitutive.

source_provisional_finding.summary: The case confirms Assisted Performance Agency but shows that the schema’s summary-level agency modes cannot fully represent when control shifts during a run. Phase-level agency segments are needed before normative attribution.

content: Task-level logs identifying control mode, pilot input, autonomous action, and failure at each phase.

classified_object.notes: The object is the BCI Race contest in which a pilot uses measured brain activity to control a computer-based vehicle or game process.

performance_agency.summary: The pilot intentionally generates brain-activity patterns during the race; decoded commands materially influence the vehicle.

performance_interface.summary: A physiological sensing interface measures brain activity and translates it into computer control.

embodied_performance.summary: The performance is biologically generated and cognitively demanding, but conventional motor expression is minimal or absent. Whether this satisfies the Spatial Athletic System embodiment condition remains unresolved.

arena.summary: The race occurs in an animated computational scenario controlled by decoded brain signals.

distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Common task software and event timing.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Participant-specific calibration is material and remains only partially comparable.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Software and officials determine task completion and ranking.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Participant fatigue and signal burden are local human limits.

sensing_tracking.summary: Brain activity is sensed and classified in real time.

measurement.summary: Decoder output, task completion, and time are measured.

comparability.summary: Signal variability, calibration, classifier design, stress, and participant-specific training complicate comparison.

officiation.summary: Competition software and officials administer task state and results.

outcome_openness.summary: Race progress depends on live pilot-generated commands and system decoding.

consequence_structure.summary: Task completion, time, ranking, and awards follow from the contest.

operational_spatial_integration.summary: Operational spatial integration is constitutive, but embodiment is category-disputed because performance is physiological and cognitive rather than conventionally motor.

human_limits_accessibility.note: Designed for severe motor impairment; fatigue and signal burden matter.

intentional_biological_control.summary: The pilot intentionally generates brain-activity patterns that are decoded into task commands. This establishes a live bodily-origin performance channel but does not by itself settle Spatial Athletic System membership.

source_provisional_finding.summary: The case cannot be reduced to an ordinary computational contest because the human biological signal is the live performance channel; nor can v0.2 yet assert that this is sufficient Embodied Performance for Spatial Athletic System membership.

content: A defensible category rule distinguishing intentional physiological performance from incidental biosignal measurement.

classified_object.notes: The object is the physical Systems Competition in which human teams design and supervise autonomous robot teams searching a physical course.

performance_agency.summary: Human design and supervisory decisions matter, but robots perform substantial autonomous navigation and search during the timed run.

performance_interface.summary: Humans interact through command systems while autonomous robots act physically in the course.

embodied_performance.summary: The decisive physical execution is robotic rather than live human bodily performance.

arena.summary: Physical subterranean courses and computational maps jointly structure robot operation and scoring.

distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Robot telemetry, maps, networking, and command systems connect the command post to the course.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Not intended as identical-system calibration; heterogeneous systems are compared through common tasks and scoring.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: DARPA validates spatial reports, timing, and ranking from the shared competition infrastructure.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Physical separation reduces direct human exposure while robot and course safety remain governed.

sensing_tracking.summary: Robots use perception, localization, networking, and mapping to detect artifacts and report locations.

measurement.summary: Correct artifact type and location within tolerance produce points; time resolves ranking.

comparability.summary: Common courses, report limits, location tolerance, and time frame support comparison, while system architectures vary by design.

officiation.summary: DARPA systems and officials validate artifact reports and scores.

outcome_openness.summary: Results emerge through team design, supervision, and autonomous system execution.

consequence_structure.summary: Points, time, ranking, and prize awards form the consequence structure.

operational_spatial_integration.summary: The competition has rich operational spatial integration, but not human athletic embodiment. It is an engineering contest outside the Spatial Athletic core.

human_limits_accessibility.note: Robots enter hazardous spaces to reduce human risk.

source_provisional_finding.summary: Operational spatial integration can be very strong without Spatial Athletic System membership. The case also confirms that agency handoff requires phase-level representation rather than one summary list.

content: Phase logs showing human commands, autonomous decisions, and causal contribution throughout each run.

classified_object.notes: The object is a historical Formula E race under the FANBOOST rule, not current Formula E and not fan voting in sport generally.

performance_agency.summary: Drivers retain live vehicle-control agency; fan votes allocate an optional power resource but do not execute the driving action.

performance_interface.summary: Driver performance is mediated by a regulated racing vehicle and controls.

embodied_performance.summary: Vehicle control, endurance, sensorimotor coordination, cognitive demand, and physiological load remain decisive.

arena.summary: The racing arena is a physical street circuit. Fan voting occurs outside the arena.

distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Voting and vehicle systems communicate resource eligibility and deployment.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Not applicable to arena distribution.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Officials and vehicle systems administer eligibility and deployment under the rule.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Motorsport safety remains separate from the voting mechanism.

sensing_tracking.summary: Vehicle telemetry and race timing measure the physical contest; fan votes determine eligibility for the boost.

measurement.summary: Race timing, position, energy, and results are measured under championship rules.

comparability.summary: The mechanism was declared equally available as a voting process, but popularity produced intentionally unequal assistance.

officiation.summary: Championship officials and vehicle systems administer legal deployment.

outcome_openness.summary: The race result remains open and driver-dependent, although spectators alter available resources.

consequence_structure.summary: Championship points and race results may be affected by the additional power resource.

operational_spatial_integration.summary: FANBOOST is a digital spectator intervention into resource allocation, not Operational Spatial Integration. L8 participation becomes constitutive without turning spectators into performance agents.

participatory_actor_relations.action_window: Official FANBOOST voting period before resource deployment.
participatory_actor_relations.mechanism: Public votes determine which eligible drivers receive an optional power resource.
participatory_actor_relations.resource_or_constraint_effect: Allocates an optional rule-authorized power resource; the driver retains deployment and driving control.
participatory_actor_relations.uncertainty: The effect on a specific race result is not quantified.

human_limits_accessibility.note: Motorsport safety remains separate from fan voting.

source_provisional_finding.summary: Spectator influence can become constitutive to resource allocation without becoming Performance Agency, officiation, or Spatiality. The ontology needs a participatory rule/resource actor relation.

content: A format in which spectators continuously execute skill-dependent actions that directly control the competitive object.
